subject.title: feat(browser): restore driver "extension" via a loopback Chrome extension relay (no remote-debugging prompt)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a bundled first-party Chrome extension relay for signed-in browser control after hardening and live proof, or defer this work to the broader browser-backend/plugin and cross-machine relay strategy?
rationale: The PR restores a security-sensitive browser-control boundary, changes public config/setup behavior, and only partially covers the canonical cross-machine regression, so automation cannot choose the permanent product and trust model.

options.title: Proceed after hardening and proof
options.body: Fix the CDP auth, Playwright target info, pairing, payload, and token-compare blockers, require live Chrome extension proof, and keep the cross-machine topology tracked separately.

options.title: Defer to browser backend API
options.body: Pause this PR until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19289 defines driver registration, extension ownership, and cross-machine relay boundaries.

options.title: Keep relay outside core
options.body: Close or replace the branch if maintainers decide signed-in Chrome extension control should live in an external plugin or platform-specific integration instead of bundled OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Proceed after hardening and proof
recommendation.body: Fix the CDP auth, Playwright target info, pairing, payload, and token-compare blockers, require live Chrome extension proof, and keep the cross-machine topology tracked separately.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the relay-removal and doctor-migration PR that established the current behavior this PR reverses.
